headline: Enterprise strength offsets a softer sequential quarter
summary_short: Revenue rose 19% y/y to $788M (down 3% q/q) as 23% growth in Enterprise Technology outpaced a 10% Service Provider Technology decline; gross margin expanded to 47% from 45% and net income grew 30% y/y to $234M ($3.86 diluted EPS).
summary_long: Revenue grew 19% y/y to $788M (though down 3% q/q) as 23% growth in Enterprise Technology outpaced a 10% decline in Service Provider Technology. Gross margin expanded to 47% from 45% on favorable product mix, lower shipping and inventory-obsolescence charges, partly offset by tariffs. Operating income rose 28% y/y to $291M as opex grew slower than revenue. Interest expense fell 88% after debt repayments, while a higher effective tax rate (19.4% vs 18.5%) partly offset gains; net income grew 30% y/y to $234M ($3.86 diluted EPS). Short-term debt fell to zero, cash rose to $369M, and the quarterly dividend held at $0.80/share. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Results were driven by strong Enterprise Technology demand across all regions and gross-margin expansion, partly offset by a Service Provider Technology decline and higher tariff costs on imports from China and Vietnam.

Enterprise Technology revenue rose 23% y/y across all regions to $717.9M; Service Provider Technology fell 10% to $70.3M, attributed to lower revenue across all regions except North America and South America.
Gross margin rose to 47% from 45% y/y on favorable product mix, lower shipping and indirect costs, and reduced excess-and-obsolete inventory charges, partly offset by higher tariff costs.
Cost of revenue grew 13% y/y, roughly tracking volume, but fell as a share of revenue (53% vs 55%) for the same mix and cost reasons cited for the gross-margin gain.
Operating income grew 28% y/y as revenue growth and margin gains outpaced a 16% rise in total opex (R&D +17% to $51.8M, SG&A +13% to $28.1M).
This shard-sourced figure tracks the same operating-income trend above; it is a third-party derivation, not the company's own non-GAAP metric.

Net income grew 30% y/y, helped by an 88% drop in interest expense (to $0.7M) after debt repayments, partly offset by a higher effective tax rate (19.4% vs 18.5%) from a shift in the geographic mix of taxable income and FDII/GILTI/Pillar Two effects.
Diluted EPS tracked the net-income gain almost exactly, since the diluted share count was essentially unchanged (60.57M vs 60.55M a year ago).

Cash built up mainly because $630.1M of nine-month operating cash flow outpaced $396.9M used in financing (including $250.0M of credit-facility repayment and $145.2M of dividends) and $14.4M of capex; not broken out by discrete quarter.
Short-term debt fell to zero after the company repaid $250.0 million outstanding under its credit facilities during the nine months ended March 31, 2026.
Equity grew mainly from retained-earnings accumulation (nine-month net income of $675.4M) net of $145.2M of dividends paid; not itemized further by the release.
